questions.question:
Choose the option that has an error in the sentence.

The more a culture expand, the less chance there is that it will become extinct.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence contains a grammatical error in the phrase "**The more a culture expand**."
 
• The verb "**expand**" should be in its singular form "**expands**" to agree with the singular subject "**a culture**."
 
• In sentences that follow this comparative structure ("The more... the less"), subject-verb agreement must be maintained for grammatical correctness.
 
• Thus, the error lies in **Option 1**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The more a culture **expands**, the less chance there is that it will become extinct."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "the less chance there is"** – This part is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 3: "that it will become extinct"** – This part is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "No correction required"** – This is incorrect because there is an error in **Option 1**.
</ul

questions.question: Choose the sentence with correct usage of "less" and "fewer".

options.text: She has less books than I do.
There are fewer sugar in the jar.
We need fewer volunteers this time.
He has fewer money than his brother.

questions.solution:
The** correct answer** is **Option 3** i.e. **We need fewer volunteers this time.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"fewer"** is used for **countable nouns** (things you can count individually, like books, people, or volunteers).** **
 
• The word **"less"** is used for **uncountable nouns** (things that are seen as a mass or bulk quantity and cannot be counted individually, like water, sugar, or air).
 
• In **Option 3**, **"volunteers"** is a countable noun, so **"fewer"** is the correct grammatical choice.

Therefore, the** correct answer** is:** Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"Books" are countable. It should be: "She has **fewer** books than I do."
 
• **Option 2: **"Sugar" is uncountable. It should be: "There is **less** sugar in the jar."
 
• **Option 4: **While we count currency, the word **"money"** itself is treated as an uncountable mass noun. It should be: "He has **less** money than his brother." (Note: You would use "fewer" for specific units, like "fewer dollars").

questions.question:
**Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition:**

The company is under investigation ____ financial irregularities.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**over**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The preposition "**over**" is commonly used to indicate the subject of an investigation, disagreement, or concern.
 
• In this sentence, "**over**" is the most appropriate choice to connect "investigation" with "financial irregularities."
 
• **Options 1 (for), 3 (on),** and **4 (about)** are incorrect in this context as they do not fit the intended meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"The company is under investigation **over**__ financial irregularities."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "for"** is incorrect as it implies a purpose or reason, which does not align with the context of an investigation.
 
• **Option 3: "on"** is incorrect as it is less commonly used to describe the subject of an investigation.
 
• **Option 4: "about"** is incorrect because it is too informal and does not fit the formal tone of the sentence.

questions.question:
**Fill in the blank with the most appropriate idiom:**

The politician's speech was full of vague promises but ultimately it was just ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. smoke and mirrors**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"smoke and mirrors"** refers to an act of deception, often to make something appear different from what it actually is. (धोखा या भ्रम उत्पन्न करने की क्रिया)
 
 
• **Example:** The company's promises of huge profits turned out to be nothing but smoke and mirrors.
 
 
• The given sentence highlights how the politician's speech was deceptive and full of illusions but lacked substance.
 
 
• **Example:** The politician's speech was full of vague promises, but ultimately it was just smoke and mirrors. (राजनेता का भाषण अस्पष्ट वादों से भरा था, लेकिन अंततः यह सिर्फ धोखा था।)
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. smoke and mirrors**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

__
 
• **Pulling strings** (रस्सियाँ खींचना): To secretly use influence or power to achieve a goal.
 
 
• **Example:** He got the job because his father was pulling strings for him. (उसे नौकरी मिली क्योंकि उसके पिता उसके लिए रस्सियाँ खींच रहे थे।)
 
 
 
 
• **A red herring** (ध्यान भटकाने वाली चीज): Something that misleads or distracts from the main issue.
 
 
• **Example:** The detective realized that the clue was just a red herring to mislead the investigation. (जासूस ने महसूस किया कि सुराग सिर्फ ध्यान भटकाने के लिए था।)
 
 
 
 
• **The last straw** (आखिरी बूँद): The final problem or difficulty that makes a situation unbearable.
 
 
• **Example:** Her rude comment was the last straw, and I decided to end the friendship. (उसकी अशिष्ट टिप्पणी आखिरी बूँद थी, और मैंने दोस्ती खत्म करने का फैसला किया।)

questions.question:

• The option "**over the canal**" is incorrect because it implies the paper boat is floating above the canal, which is contextually inappropriate.
 
• The phrase "**No substitution**" is incorrect because the original sentence lacks the directional clarity provided by "**down the canal**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"I watched the paper boat float **down the canal**__ towards the lake."*

• **Option 4: "No substitution"** is incorrect since the original sentence lacks clarity and needs improvement for precision.

questions.question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

The officer said, "The library will be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month."

options.text: The officer said that the library would be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.
The officer said that the library must be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.
The officer said that the library has to be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.
The officer said that the library ought to be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The sentence provided is in indirect speech, where the reporting verb "said" has been used.
 
• **Key Conversion:**
 
 
• The direct speech, "The library will be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month," is converted to indirect speech by changing "will" to "would" to maintain the sequence of tenses.
 
• The phrase "the library will be supplied" becomes "the library would be supplied" in indirect narration.
 
• The rest of the sentence remains the same as it does not require additional changes for accurate indirect narration.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• In indirect speech, quotation marks are removed.
 
• The sentence is restructured with the reporting verb followed by the indirect statement.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** The officer said that the library would be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** The officer said that the library must be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.
 
 
• Incorrect as "must" changes the modality and meaning of the sentence, implying an obligation rather than a statement of future supply.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** The officer said that the library has to be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.
 
 
• Incorrect as "has to be supplied" uses present tense, which does not align with the past reporting verb "said."
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** The officer said that the library ought to be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.
 
 
• Incorrect as "ought to be supplied" changes the tone of the statement, indicating a suggestion or moral obligation rather than a factual statement.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**Change the following sentence into the Active form.**

The report is being reviewed by the manager.

options.text: The report is reviewing the manager.
The manager is reviewing the report.
The manager had reviewed the report.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• To convert a sentence from passive voice to active voice, the subject of the passive sentence becomes the object in the active sentence, and the object of the passive sentence becomes the subject.
 
• The given sentence in the passive voice is: "The report is being reviewed by the manager."
 
• Here, "The report" is the subject in the passive sentence, and "the manager" is the agent performing the action.
 
• To convert it to active voice, make "the manager" the subject and "the report" the object.
 
• The verb form "is being reviewed" in the passive voice is changed to "is reviewing" in the active voice to maintain the present continuous tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The manager is reviewing the report."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The manager reviews the report." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to present simple instead of maintaining the present continuous tense.
 
• **Option 2: **"The report is reviewing the manager." – Incorrect because it reverses the roles of the subject and object, leading to an illogical sentence.
 
• **Option 4: **"The manager had reviewed the report." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to past perfect instead of present continuous.

3d:T

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

He begged me to give him another chance.

options.text: He said, "Please give me another chance."
He begged me, "Can you give me another chance?"
He begged, "I need another chance please."
He said to me, "You should give me another chance."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** The sentence is converted from indirect speech to direct speech while keeping the meaning intact.
 
• **Correct Conversion:**
 
 
• **Indirect Speech:** "He begged me to give him another chance."
 
• **Direct Speech:** "He said, "Please give me another chance.""
 
• Here, the word "begged" is appropriately represented by "Please" in the direct speech format.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• The word "Please" conveys the request tone effectively.
 
• The reporting clause, "He said," is placed before the quoted speech and is followed by a comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He said, "Please give me another chance.""*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "He begged me, "Can you give me another chance?""
 
 
• This option changes the tone of the sentence from a request to a question, which is inaccurate.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He begged, "I need another chance please.""
 
 
• This option alters the structure of the original sentence and does not accurately convey the request tone.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He said to me, "You should give me another chance.""
 
 
• This option changes the meaning of the original sentence by turning it into a suggestion rather than a request.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

The sun is shining bright **__but __**it will be possible to go out for a walk.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**1**' i.e. 'so'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The highlighted sentence describes a cause-and-effect relationship between two clauses: **"The sun is shining bright"** (cause) and **"it will be possible to go out for a walk"** (effect).
 
• The correct conjunction to establish this cause-and-effect relationship is **"so."**
 
• **Options 2, 3**, and **4** do not fit the context:
 
 
• **Option 2: "while"** is used to indicate simultaneous actions or contrast, which is not the case here.
 
• **Option 3: "when"** is used to refer to a specific time, which is irrelevant in this context.
 
• **Option 4: "hence"** is used to indicate a conclusion, but it does not fit the sentence grammatically.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The sun is shining bright, so it will be possible to go out for a walk."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "while"** is used to show simultaneous actions or contrast, such as "While I was cooking, she was reading."
 
• **Option 3: "when"** is used to refer to a specific time, such as "I was happy when I won the prize."
 
• **Option 4: "hence"** is used to indicate a conclusion but cannot replace "so" grammatically in this sentence.
</ul

questions.question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

The highly anticipated sequel to the blockbuster movie will have been produced by the esteemed director.

options.text: The esteemed director will have produced the highly anticipated sequel to the blockbuster movie.
The esteemed director will produce the highly anticipated sequel to the blockbuster movie.
The esteemed director has produced the highly anticipated sequel to the blockbuster movie.
The esteemed director will be producing the highly anticipated sequel to the blockbuster movie.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence ("...will have been produced by...") is in the **passive voice** (Future Perfect Passive).
 
• To transform it into the **active voice**, the agent following "by" (the esteemed director) becomes the subject.
 
• The verb form must change from "will have been produced" (passive) to **"will have produced"** (active) to maintain the **Future Perfect** tense.
 
• The original subject ("The highly anticipated sequel...") becomes the direct object of the active sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence (Active):** *"The esteemed director will have produced the highly anticipated sequel to the blockbuster movie."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"The esteemed director will produce..." – Incorrect tense (Future Simple).
 
• **Option 3: **"The esteemed director has produced..." – Incorrect tense (Present Perfect).
 
• **Option 4: **"The esteemed director will be producing..." – Incorrect tense (Future Continuous).

questions.question:
“Mental health has emerged as a crucial component of an adult’s overall well-being”.

Rewrite the sentence as a negative sentence without changing its meaning.

options.text: Mental health has not failed to emerge as a crucial component of an adult’s overall well-being.
Mental health has not emerged as a crucial component of an adult’s overall well-being.
Mental health doesn’t emerge as a crucial component of an adult’s overall well-being.
Mental health never emerged as a crucial component of an adult’s overall well-being.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1: Mental health has not failed to emerge...***

 
 
• To change an affirmative sentence into a negative one without changing its meaning, we often use a **double negative** or an antonym.
 
• The phrase "has not failed to emerge" is logically equivalent to "has emerged." By using "not" + "failed," the sentence becomes grammatically negative while maintaining the original factual statement.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Mental health has not emerged...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect** because it directly contradicts the original passage. It changes the meaning from "it is a component" to "it is not a component."
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Mental health doesn’t emerge...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Similar to Option 2, it changes the meaning to a negative fact. Additionally, it changes the tense from Present Perfect ("has emerged") to Simple Present ("doesn't emerge").
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Mental health never emerged...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. It changes the meaning to suggest that the event never happened at all, which is the opposite of the author's intent.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transformation Rules**: When converting Affirmative to Negative without changing meaning: 

 
 
• Use **Not + Antonym**: (e.g., "He is a good boy" becomes "He is *not a bad* boy").
 
• Use **Double Negatives**: (e.g., "I remember you" becomes "I do *not forget* you").
 
 
 
• **Context**: In the passage, the author highlights mental health as a positive, emerging priority. Option 1 is the only one that upholds this perspective while satisfying the grammatical requirement for a negative word ("not").

questions.question:
**Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:**

P. He heated a bar of steel in the forge until it glowed a bright, brilliant orange.

Q. He hammered the hot metal on the anvil, shaping it into the form he desired.

R. He tempered the finished piece, dipping it in oil to give it strength and durability.

S. The forged object was a strong, beautiful piece, born of fire and brute force.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
 
• The given sentences describe the process of forging a strong, beautiful piece of metal, and the sequence must reflect the logical order of actions in the process. 
 
• **Sentence P** is the first step in the process, where the steel is heated in the forge until it glows bright orange: 
 
 
• "He heated a bar of steel in the forge until it glowed a bright, brilliant orange." 
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q** follows as the second step, where the hot metal is hammered and shaped on the anvil: 
 
 
• "He hammered the hot metal on the anvil, shaping it into the form he desired." 
 
 
 
• **Sentence S** comes next as the third step, where the forged object is described as a strong and beautiful piece, reflecting the result of the forging process: 
 
 
• "The forged object was a strong, beautiful piece, born of fire and brute force." 
 
 
 
• **Sentence R** is the final step, where the finished piece is tempered in oil to enhance its strength and durability: 
 
 
• "He tempered the finished piece, dipping it in oil to give it strength and durability." 
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **P, Q, S, R**. 

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"He heated a bar of steel in the forge until it glowed a bright, brilliant orange. He hammered the hot metal on the anvil, shaping it into the form he desired. The forged object was a strong, beautiful piece, born of fire and brute force. He tempered the finished piece, dipping it in oil to give it strength and durability."</div
